Definition: or Μαριάμ of Hebrew origin (H4813); Maria or Mariam (i.e. Mirjam), the name of six Christian females:-- Mary.
BiblicalUsage: María is Mary, the name of six women in the New Testament, and this study follows the name rather than one life. In John 11:1 Mary of Bethany is named with her sister Martha, and in John 11:20 Mary sits still in the house while Martha goes to meet Jesus. In John 19:25 Mary the mother of Jesus stands by the cross with Mary Magdalene., and each Mary's story lives on her own People profile.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe María shows me that God works through ordinary women who believe Him, and I hold that the mother who stood by the cross and the sister who sat at His feet both belong in the story.
RelatedPeople: Mary, Mother of Jesus; Mary Magdalene; Mary of Bethany
